liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Same Thing** (3 reviews): Pigpen's performance of this is called an obvious highlight of the tape; Described as one of the most exploratory versions of this song ever [7][11][16]
- **Dancin' In The Street** (2 reviews, 1 other source): The upgraded transfer includes the Dancin' In The Street played that night; Some listings place it as the first-set closer, with Cold Rain And Snow opening and Hi-Heel Sneakers next [1][6][15]
- **Cold Rain And Snow** (1 review): The band really starts cranking around this song and stays hot afterward [11]
- **Hi-Heel Sneakers** (1 other source): Played only a few years after Tommy Tucker's original recording; described as a spitfire performance [19]
- **Pain In My Heart** (1 review): Reviewer believes the band played this song only twice in total [12]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 review): Reviewer especially enjoyed this performance [16]
- **Smokestack Lightnin'** (1 review): Smokestack into King Bee is singled out for standout Pigpen performances [7]
- **I'm A King Bee** (1 review): Reviewer especially enjoyed the King Bee [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Hi-Heel Sneakers**: rare: 5 archived performances [17]
- **Pain In My Heart**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [17]
- **Cream Puff War**: rare: 12 archived performances [17]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Smokestack Lightnin' [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-11-19.sbd.miller.94106.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 11 songs; 80 min; rated 4.3/5 by 20 [1]
- **gd1966-11-19.fm.9730.shnf**: FM broadcast; 11 songs; 79 min; rated 4/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd66-11-19.sbd.seff.41.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 70 min; rated 4.55/5 by 31 [3]. Said about its sound: The mix is described as very clean, good for headphone listening; Sound quality is good but not great; Sound quality is rated around three out of five, decent for a 1966 tape [8][11][15]
- **gd1966-11-19.sbd.seff-joshd.41-speed-fixed.75970.flacf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 72 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [4]. Said about its sound: Uploader says it sounds pretty good for the show's age [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer considers it the single best tape to pick from 1966 [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-11-19.sbd.miller.94106.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel [1]. Also: Miller soundboard transfer; slight overburn was needed to fit everything on one disc [1]
- **gd1966-11-19.fm.9730.shnf**: source: KSAN [2]. Also: Part of the KSAN vaults collection, 1966-1968, on six CDs; partially broadcast on KSAN [2]
- **gd66-11-19.sbd.seff.41.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: A better-sounding copy circulates than the listed one; the upgrade fixes the setlist order; Liberated bootleg source, with extraction and SHN encoding done by Jon Seff [3][6]
- **gd1966-11-19.sbd.seff-joshd.41-speed-fixed.75970.flacf**: source: FM [4]. Also: Liberated bootleg; hum at 16khz reduced with an FFT filter in Cool Edit Pro, then FLAC encoded [4]
